subject: Dedicated GPU pool — strategic pricing escalation (DataSphere)

Subject: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & price question — next steps

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at DataSphere is excited about the latency and KV cache behavior you showed. We ran through budgets with procurement this morning and have a few concrete asks before we can move to legal:

- We need a committed GPU pool sized for 12xA10 equivalent capacity (steady throughput target ~650 tokens/sec).
- Can Redwood commit to 99th percentile latency <= 120ms for average prompt lengths (we'll share sample prompts)?
- Pricing: your pricing sheet shows $X/unit for reserved commits. Competitor Y has offered a 25%-off match plus three months free. Is there room for Redwood to provide any strategic pricing/credits for an initial 12-month reserved commit?

Procurement attached some of their procurement templates and asked for a quick mutual action plan. I attached a one-page SOW for your reference.

Appreciate any flexibility — want to get to terms this quarter.

Emma

Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for the clear asks. I looped in Rishi (AE) to help with commercial specifics. Quick answers up front:

- Pool sizing: 12 A10-equivalent is doable; we recommend a config mapping to 2x 8-GPU nodes with shared KV cache to meet your throughput target.
- Latency SLO: 99p <= 120ms is achievable if we enable continuous batching thresholds you described; we'll validate on your prompt set during onboarding.
- Pricing/credits: we don't publish ad-hoc discounts from the AE level — will need an approval for any strategic concession.

Next steps I suggest: Rishi to propose a pricing counter (list price, proposed discount, and a 12-month reserved commit structure), then we can escalate to our sales leader if we need to match the competitor offer. If you can share the competitor pricing spreadsheet and your preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly), that will speed things up.

I'll also attach our base pricing sheet so procurement has line items.

Best,
Olga

Emma / Olga — looping in Lauren since this looks like a strategic account and the ask is a list-price match + 3 months free. I'm proposing the following commercial starting point to streamline approval:

- 12-month reserved commit, billed quarterly, target = 12 A10-equivalent steady capacity.
- Commercial proposal: 20% standard discount off list + 2 months free usage credit in month 1-2 (applied as dollar credit).
- If we need to be more competitive (match 25%), we should consider a one-time onboarding credit (12% credit) plus a commitment to a 24-month renewal at a baseline floor price.

Numbers:
- List ARR for configuration: $720k/year (example)
- 20% discount -> $576k/year
- 2-month credit -> ~ $96k applied first billing year

Lauren — can you advise if we have latitude for a one-time onboarding credit for strategic accounts and whether matching 25% requires VP approval? Also confirm whether offering a 24-month renewal floor is acceptable from a legal/finance standpoint.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & price question — escalation request

Team — forwarding the thread and my recommended approval ask for Vivek:

Summary: DataSphere is a high-visibility prospect in fintech Insights; they asked us to match Competitor Y (25% off + 3 months free). We can meet them competitively with a structured concession that preserves long-term economics. Proposed concession:

1) Pricing: match 25% off list for a 12-month reserved commit (billing quarterly).
2) Credits: provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 8% of first-year committed spend (applied across first two invoices).
3) Contractual: require a 12-month initial term with an optional 12-month renewal at a no-greater-discount floor (maintain minimum ARR).
4) SLA: commit to 99p latency <= 120ms on sample prompts; include a performance review at 30/90 days.

Rationale: competitive match likely required to close this quarter. The onboarding credit is time-limited and tied to signatures by EoQ. We avoid a perpetual higher discount by tying the renewal floor. Financial impact estimate: one-time revenue give of ~10-12% on year 1 but increases likelihood of a multi-year deal + potential expansion.

Vivek — can you approve this concession structure (match 25% + 8% onboarding credit) for DataSphere, or do you want to adjust credit % / renewal conditions? If yes, please confirm so we can send an updated commercial redline to Emma and procurement.

Thanks,
Lauren
Head of North America Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & price question — escalation request

Lauren — approved with conditions. I support matching Competitor Y's 25% discount for the 12-month reserved commit plus an onboarding credit, but set the onboarding credit at 8% max of first-year committed spend as you proposed. Conditions:

- Credit to be one-time only; cannot be applied to renewals.
- Require DataSphere to sign by 2026-09-30 to qualify for the onboarding credit.
- Legal to add a renewal-price-floor clause: renewal discount cannot exceed the initial discount unless reviewed by NA sales leadership.
- Include a performance review clause at 30/90 days; if we fail to meet the 99p latency SLO in that window, apply an SLA credit schedule (standard template).

Lauren/Rishi/Olga — proceed to update the commercial redline and send to Emma. Copy Finance on the final contract before DocuSign.

Vivek

VP Sales | Redwood Inference
